name: ICM | List Profiles
fixtures: records/eligibility-probe.json - seed with: node scripts/ua-records.mjs seed records/eligibility-probe.json --env tool
note: Covers the commissionEligible join added 2026-09-09. Spec:
The probe row's window is HISTORICAL (2020) on purpose, so the suite can
assert a `false` without any date the product actually reports being
affected. Ask as of today and the row is out of force; ask as of 2020 and it
is the answer. That also makes the interesting assertion possible: not that
false is honoured, but that a window which ENDED stops applying. A flat
boolean on Payee cannot fail that test, because it has no window to end -
which is the entire reason eligibility is a dated table.
Read-only: creates and deletes nothing, safe to re-run.
asOfDate is sent EMPTY for the today cases rather than a literal date, so the
suite does not start failing the day someone runs it in a different month.

cases.name: eligibility: no row in force resolves to ELIGIBLE
cases.note: The default, and the whole risk of this change. Every person on the platform has no row, so a default of false would have told the app that nobody in the company is on a variable plan.

cases.name: eligibility: a row IN FORCE makes the person ineligible, with its reason

checks.equals: KITFIX probe: proves the dated window is obeyed

cases.name: eligibility: a window that ENDED no longer applies
cases.note: THE case. This is the March question the design doc's rule 4 exists for, and the only one that distinguishes a dated table from an overwritable flag. If this returns false, the join is ignoring effectiveEnd and every historical answer is wrong.

cases.name: eligibility: a window that has NOT STARTED does not apply either
cases.note: The other end of the window. Without this, a join that only checked effectiveEnd would pass every case above.

cases.name: the join added a field and did not drop rows
cases.note: A join wired wrong is as likely to shrink the page as to return the wrong value, and a page that silently loses people is the worse failure. Asserts the shape the automation had BEFORE eligibility existed.

cases.name: an unusable request is still refused
cases.note: Eligibility must not have moved the failure path. This is the automation's own pre-existing contract, asserted here because nothing else covered it.
